# Permissions

The IAM policy and Kubernetes RBAC that `aws-enumerator` needs, generated from the actions every collector declares in its registry `SPEC`. The CLI prints the same documents, offline, for the modules and flags you select: `aws-enumerator permissions` (IAM JSON), `--format k8s` (RBAC YAML) or `--format markdown` (both, plus the actions per module); selection and options: `--modules`, `--skip`, `--max-tier 1`, `--no-k8s`, `--k8s-secrets`, `--partition`, `--include-optional`, `--guardrail`.

## IAM policy

[reference/iam-policy.json](reference/iam-policy.json) is the output of `aws-enumerator permissions` with the default selection (every module, Kubernetes on, tier 2, partition `aws`): 165 actions of 32 services. Every action is a `List*`, `Describe*` or `Get*` read except `apigateway:GET`, `iam:GenerateCredentialReport`.

| Statement | Effect | Actions | Resource | Included |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AwsEnumeratorTier1` | Allow | 142 | `*` | always |
| `AwsEnumeratorApiGatewayRead` | Allow | 1 | 4 API Gateway ARNs | always (API Gateway modules) |
| `AwsEnumeratorTier2SecretBearingConfig` | Allow | 22 | `*` | unless `--max-tier 1` |
| `AwsEnumeratorOptional` | Allow | 36 | `*` | only with `--include-optional` |
| `AwsEnumeratorDenyDataPlane` | Deny | 19 | `*` | only with `--guardrail` |

Tier-2 modules (`cloudformation`, `codebuild`, `ecs`, `glue`, `lambda`) call APIs whose answers can contain secret-bearing configuration; `--max-tier 1` drops them and their statement. `apigateway:GET` is scoped to the REST/HTTP API resources the collector reads, because a blanket `apigateway:GET` on `*` would also read API key values.

## Kubernetes RBAC

[reference/k8s-clusterrole.yaml](reference/k8s-clusterrole.yaml) is the output of `aws-enumerator permissions --format k8s`: a `ClusterRole` (`list` `namespaces`, `nodes`, `pods`, `serviceaccounts`, `services` (core); `create` `selfsubjectrulesreviews` (authorization.k8s.io); `list` `ingresses` (networking.k8s.io); `list` `clusterrolebindings`, `clusterroles`, `rolebindings`, `roles` (rbac.authorization.k8s.io)), a `kube-system` `Role` that can only `get` the `aws-auth` ConfigMap, and bindings of both to the Kubernetes group `aws-enumerator-readers` (map the scanning IAM role to that group, for example with an EKS access entry). Secrets are not listed by default; with `--k8s-secrets` the tool asks for Secret metadata only, but the `list secrets` RBAC it then needs lets that identity read every Secret value.

## Compared with SecurityAudit

Many teams start from the AWS managed policy `SecurityAudit`. These actions of the generated policy are not in it, so a run with SecurityAudit alone records them as denied (the module's coverage shows it):

| Action | Used by module |
|---|---|
| `eks:DescribeAddon` | `eks` |
| `eks:ListAddons` | `eks` |
| `wafv2:GetIPSet` | `waf_cloudfront`, `waf` |
| `wafv2:GetRuleGroup` | `waf_cloudfront`, `waf` |

Source: AWS managed policy SecurityAudit, version 94 (AWS managed policy reference, page edited 2026-09-30), compared during the review of finding F-151. The comparison is data in `scripts/gen_docs.py` and is not refreshed automatically; AWS revises the managed policy, and modules added after that review (for example `guardduty`, `securityhub`, `config`, `accessanalyzer`, `organizations`) were not compared. To check the current version yourself, compare the generated policy with `aws iam get-policy-version --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/SecurityAudit --version-id <default version>`. Granting the generated policy (or SecurityAudit plus the actions above) avoids the gap.

## Guardrail (`--guardrail`)

Adds an explicit `Deny` on data-plane reads the tool never needs, so that a policy widened by mistake still cannot read object contents, secret values, parameters or messages: `dynamodb:BatchGetItem`, `dynamodb:GetItem`, `dynamodb:Query`, `dynamodb:Scan`, `ecr:BatchGetImage`, `ecr:GetDownloadUrlForLayer`, `kms:Decrypt`, `lambda:GetFunction`, `lambda:InvokeFunction`, `logs:FilterLogEvents`, `logs:GetLogEvents`, `s3:GetObject`, `s3:GetObjectVersion`, `secretsmanager:GetSecretValue`, `sqs:ReceiveMessage`, `ssm:GetParameter`, `ssm:GetParameterHistory`, `ssm:GetParameters`, `ssm:GetParametersByPath`.

## Pre-flight

`aws-enumerator preflight` (or `collect --preflight`, `collect --preflight-only`) checks the selected modules before a run. `--mode probe` (default) makes one cheap read per module; `--mode simulate` asks `iam:SimulatePrincipalPolicy` about every action. **Probes are real API calls and appear in CloudTrail.** The exit code is 0 when every module is allowed (or skipped), 2 otherwise, and 1 when the credentials do not work.
